coaching.headline: One hero beat us: Revenant went 19/4 with 37k damage and took seven of our eight caught-alone deaths — armor into him was the missing answer.
coaching.team: Four lanes read favored and the game still ended 1-10 on towers, because we fed a single carry the whole film. Revenant finished 19/4/2 with 37k physical damage; of our eight deaths outside any fight (they gave up two), seven were his, five of them Drongo. Their conversion was ruthless and ours was not — they cashed 4 of their 5 won fights, we cashed 1 of 3 — so every loss became map: the 13.6 fight (0-3, taken while the winning mid was absent and the offlane was pinned) became three outer towers by 15.0, the 14.9 loss (taken while mid and support were alive and ahead elsewhere) handed over Fangtooth at 15.9, the 21-minute 0-4 at their inner tower became the inner (21.7) and Fangtooth again (22.1), and the pickoffs at 22.8 and 24.3 became Orb Prime (23) and the inhibitor cascade (25.2-25.5). Two fixes travel to the next game: build armor when one physical carry has all the kills, and stop crossing the map alone once he's fed. Objective damage tells the rest: 8986 to their 42404.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The 21-minute fight at their inner tower: four of us, with a modeled 8-to-4 item lead, lost 0-4 to Revenant and Mourn alone — and it bought them the inner tower (21.7) and Fangtooth (22.1). From there every catch cashed: Orb Prime at 23 off the 22.8 pickoff, the inhibitors at 25.2-25.5 off the 24.3 pickoff, core at 25.9 after the last 2-5.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31 won mid all game on the exact winning build (Combustion, Wraith Leggings, Megacosm). The gap was where the lead went: The Fey was alive and ahead but absent from both the 13.6 and 14.9 losses at their outer tower — the macro read says a shove-and-rotate flips each — and the 22.8 solo catch by Revenant was followed by their Orb Prime at 23. In this game the winning mid's job was to show up to the fights the losing half of the map kept taking.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 drew the one unfavored lane and Grux got pinned — theirs all game with 7166 hero damage — which the macro read kept flagging: several team fights were the wrong call because the offlane was stuck across the map. The costly beat was the 24.3 catch by Revenant, which preceded both inner towers (24.8, 24.9) and all three inhibitor hits (25.2-25.5). Behind in a lost lane, the play is safety and utility — Basilisk was the missing core piece, and the 24-minute death was the one Grux could not afford.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster won the support matchup and placed 13 wards, but Dekker kept dying in the wrong fights: in the 10.6 loss at our Fangtooth (0-3 to Revenant, alone, on their side of the kill feed), at 14.0 just before two outer towers fell, at 21.3 in the 0-4, and at 25.7 before the core. When three of us are losing to one Revenant, the stun is worth more as peel on our side of the map than as an engage into him.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim's lane read favored all game and Drongo still finished 5/9 — five of the nine deaths came alone outside any fight (3.5, 5.3, 6, 11.5, 18.8), four of those to Revenant. That solo-death pattern is most of the Revenant 19-kill story, and the 13.6 death preceded three outer towers falling by 15.0. The build note is secondary but real — Lightning Hawk, the missing core piece, never came. The habit fix is first: after laning, the carry moves with the support or not at all.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs died 8 times on Serath with 18240 mitigated, much of it into a Revenant the team had almost no armor for. The cost sheet ties the deaths at 14, 14.9, 21.1 and 25.3 to towers or Fangtooth, and the 14.9 fight at their outer tower was taken two-strong while mid and support were alive and ahead elsewhere. Against a 19-kill carry the jungle counts numbers before engaging — and Storm Breaker, the missing core piece, was the difference in those duels.

threats: Chain-CC risk (3 hard-CC abilities, ~1.5s of lockdown): Mourn Abduct (pull), Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback), Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Mourn. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

lines: Lead story: Stayed alive, joined every fight, and each takedown sped up the ultimate. In 75% of the team's kills (more than 98% of Revenant carry players this patch) and died 4 times (fewer than about 60% of them). Lotus turned 21 takedowns into ability haste, so Reckoning came back every ~78s instead of 110s.
Lesson: takedowns were the fuel. Each one Revenant touched shortened Reckoning, so feeding early made it come back faster (about 77.5s late); fight right after Reckoning is spent.
Reckoning at rank 3: 110s base, about 77.5s by the end (30% shorter) from 42 ability haste: Malady 8, Lotus 34.
21 takedowns (19 kills, 2 assists) fed: Malady (Demise), Lotus (Eternal).
Revenant dealt 37,010 hero damage, 43% of their team's, with +207 physical power from items.

Penetration: Malady 11, Vanquisher 12; against Drongo (level 14: about 86 physical armor, 63 after penetration; took 13,894 physical damage from heroes, 74% of all hero damage they took) and Serath (level 14: about 93 physical armor, 70 after penetration; took 12,334 physical damage from heroes, 74% of all hero damage they took) that is about 14% and 14% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).

Stack (Kept alive in fights): 4 effects on one trigger: Malady, Terminus, Pacifier, Lotus. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.
Stack (Every takedown fed): 2 effects on one trigger: Malady, Lotus. Each kill or assist made the next fight easier.
Stack (Finishing damage on low-health targets): 2 effects on one trigger: Malady, Vanquisher. Once a fight started going their way, these finished it.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 2 effects on one trigger: Terminus, Pacifier.
The Eternal was part of it: Lotus (Masterpiece + Fragrance) sits on the same triggers as the items (kept alive in fights; every takedown fed), so the same hits paid out twice.

Copy it? Lotus: 54.4% in 1,517 Revenant carry games, above the hero's 51%. Proven this patch: worth copying.

loadout.name: Spectral Bounty
loadout.text: Reckoning now grants 3x Bounty Hunter gold and 4 (+25% of stolen stats) Physical & Magical Power on Kill.

ability.name: Bounty Hunter
ability.what: Revenant's Physical Power is increased by 3/3.5/4/4.5/5/5.5/6/6.5/7/7.5/8/8.5/9/9.5/10/10.5/11/11.5% (+1% per 10% Critical Strike Chance)(+2% per 10% Bonus Attack Speed).

loadout.plain: Kills inside Reckoning pay more Bounty Hunter gold and permanent power. Use Reckoning to isolate a target you can actually kill so the reward snowballs.

loadout.name: Lotus
loadout.text: Every 2 minutes and every Takedown randomly grants +1% Damage, +4 Ability Haste, +0.75% Move Speed, or +1.25% Max Health.
numbers: 34 random bonuses this game (every 2 min plus 21 takedowns), 1 in 4 each: about +8.5% damage, about +34 ability haste, about +6.4% move speed, about +10.6% max health (expected)
loadout.plain: Every couple of minutes and every takedown, a random small stat bonus. Generic scaling with nothing special for his kit.

loadout.name: Masterpiece
loadout.text: Kills grant 4% Bonus Damage and 5% Movement Speed for 12s, stacking up to 5 times.
loadout.plain: Kills grant stacking damage and move speed for a while. It helps chain kills in fights, especially with Reckoning picks.

loadout.name: Fragrance
loadout.text: Deal 4% increased Magical Damage and 12% increased True Damage to Enemy Heroes within 800 units.
loadout.plain: More magical and true damage to nearby heroes. Revenant deals physical damage, so this does almost nothing for him.

loadout.name: Pacifier
loadout.text: Adrenalize:  Dash a short distance. Empower your next Physical Damage Instance within 3s. Deals 30 (+25%) Damage. Increased by 2.5x against Targets below 20% Max Health. Killing a Hero within 3s allows Adrenalize to be recast for 6s.
loadout.plain: A short dash that empowers your next physical hit, much stronger on a target below 20% health. Dash and fire your final round to execute, and a kill lets you recast it.

lead.title: Stayed alive, joined every fight, and each takedown sped up the ultimate
lead.text: In 75% of the team's kills (more than 98% of Revenant carry players this patch) and died 4 times (fewer than about 60% of them). Lotus turned 21 takedowns into ability haste, so Reckoning came back every ~78s instead of 110s.
